![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14219165/assets/c1bf9d989f1fbaeda90325b924f2c9285cd4e37e1948ba63256258b0a84c7e44.png)

Find the arc length of the polar curve $r={2}^{\theta }$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above).
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r={2}^{\theta },$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }={2}^{\theta }\operatorname{ln}⁡2.
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{({2}^{\theta })}^{2}+{({2}^{\theta }\operatorname{ln}⁡2)}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{2}^{2\theta }+{2}^{2\theta }{ln}^{2}⁡2}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{(1+{ln}^{2}⁡2){2}^{2\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{2}^{\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡2}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot {2}^{\theta }{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡2}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot ({2}^{\pi /2}-{2}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡2}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}({2}^{\pi /2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$
